title: Granular Source Provenance Cost Mapper
creator: Marco Li
description:
Purpose: build a standalone service that attaches fine-grained provenance metadata to token/embedding usage events and produces deterministic per-customer, per-route, and per-model cost allocations suitable for billing, chargeback, and downstream analytics. This service (Cost Mapper) will consume normalized usage events, enrich them with model perf/cost profiles and routing metadata, apply allocation rules (prefix-based, route-weighted, and burst attribution), and emit idempotent ledger entries and attribution deltas for reconciliation and billing ingestion.

Goals and acceptance criteria:
1) Deterministic mapping: identical input stream + rules => identical output ledger entries; support replay for backfills.
2) Low-latency path for near-realtime reporting: < 30s 95th latency for single-event attribution in the streaming lane.
3) Batch reconciliation: support epochal nightly aggregate job that produces per-customer deltas and a reconciled checksum.
4) Auditability: every output entry must include provenance fields (ingest_offset, source_stream, route_id, model_version, quantization_profile) and a replay_token for idempotent reprocessing.
5) Integrations: direct sink to billing-ledger topic and an append-only audit log (Kafka topic + long-term retention for forensic needs).
6) Backfill and correction support: support retroactive corrections with a controlled compensating-entry pattern and a reconciler that can mark corrections.
7) Operational SLOs: <1% of events in error state per day, monitoring alerts for drift vs expected cost-per-token by model.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Two-path architecture: streaming fast-path for production traffic (Kafka transcoders -> Cost Mapper stream processor -> ledger topic) and batch path for heavy backfills/corrections (Spark/beam job that writes the same ledger format). This preserves deterministic semantics while allowing throughput optimizations per path.
- Enrichment join strategy: perform a mostly-static join against a model profile cache (memory + TTL refresh from config-service) to avoid hot lookups, falling back to on-demand lookup for new model variants. Risk: cache staleness; mitigations include versioned model profiles and change-events that trigger cache invalidation.
- Allocation rules will be expressed as a small DSL (JSON rules) stored in config-service. We'll start with route-weighted and prefix-based rules and iterate. DSL keeps logic out of code for faster product changes but requires validation tooling to avoid bad rules.
- Idempotency: each consumed event will be normalized to a canonical key (source_stream + offset + event_hash). Output entries include an output_id derived from canonical key + applied_rule_set_hash to allow safe retries.
- Cost model: unit costs will be derived from runtime profiles (cost-per-token by model/quant profile) plus per-route overhead. We will store model cost snapshots per-day to make nightly aggregates reproducible.

Plan and milestones:
- Spike (complete) => prototype streaming processor using Kafka Streams and a simple model-profile cache. Verified deterministic outputs on small replay.
- Implementation (in progress) => full rule engine, idempotency layer, sinks to ledger topic + audit topic.
- QA & load testing => compare outputs vs existing ad-hoc mapper on synthetic traffic and a 7-day replay. Target parity +/- 0.5% before cutover.
- Cutover & monitoring => staged cutover (shadow -> canary -> primary) with checksum-based end-to-end comparison and roll-forward/rollback hooks.

Deliverables:
- Streaming Cost Mapper service (Go + Kafka Streams wrapper) with config-driven rules.
- Batch reconciliation job that emits reconciled deltas and a checksum file for each epoch.
- Schema docs for attribution ledger (avro + Confluent registry) and an append-only audit topic retention policy.
- Runbook for corrections and reconciliation failures.

comments: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: alignment meeting with PM (Samira Gomez) and Billing SME (Evan Brooks). Decided on two-path architecture and JSON DSL for allocation rules.

2026-02-28 - Spike results: Kafka Streams prototype produced deterministic ledger entries on replay. Initial performance ok at ~5k events/s on dev cluster. Follow-up: test high-cardinality customer distribution.

2026-03-03 - Design review (ENG/PM/Observability): agreed to include replay_token and output_id for idempotency and to expose per-rule metrics to Console dashboard. Action: add metrics hooks and tracing.
2026-03-06 - Implementation started: core stream processor and rule engine scaffolding pushed. Branch: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/tree/feat/cost-mapper. (PR opened soon)

2026-03-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4521 - initial streaming processor + unit tests. Requesting review from @dylan and @leah. Note: still missing audit-topic sink and schema registration.

2026-03-11 - Integration tests: discovered ordering edge-case when route-weighted rules overlap with prefix rules causing double attribution. Mitigation: rule-merge priority added and test vectors updated. Blocker for canary until fixed.

2026-03-12 - Today's status: blocker fixed in branch; smoke tests pass on staging. Preparing load test harness to run 24h replay and validate parity with legacy mapper. Next: run parity job and surface per-customer diffs to PM dashboard.
Follow-ups: coordinate with Finance to validate invoice samples post-cutover; add long-term audit topic retention (90d -> 365d proposal) and get approval from Storage team.
